title: The Green Sofa
那張綠色沙發
paras: By ten on Saturday morning, the {{showroom|showroom}} at Harbor Home was full. Nina Torres, the store manager, had planned this end-of-summer sale for weeks. The patio sets were {{seasonal|seasonal}} items, and she wanted them gone before the first cold week. Every {{shopper|shopper}} who walked in seemed to be looking for a bargain.
週六早上十點，港灣家居的展示間已經擠滿了人。店長妮娜．托雷斯為這場夏末特賣籌備了好幾個星期。庭院桌椅屬於季節性商品，她希望在第一波冷空氣來臨前把它們賣光。走進店裡的每位顧客，看起來都是來找便宜貨的。

Tom and Jess walked down the main {{aisle|aisle}} and stopped in front of a green {{sofa|sofa}}. A yellow {{sticker|sticker}} on the arm said $899, but the sale sign beside it said $699. "Which one is right?" Jess asked. A young {{clerk|clerk}} named Omar checked his tablet. "The sale price is right. The sticker is old. Sorry about that."
湯姆和潔絲沿著主走道走，在一張綠色沙發前停了下來。扶手上的黃色貼紙寫著八百九十九美元，但旁邊的特價牌卻寫六百九十九。「哪一個才對？」潔絲問。一位名叫歐馬的年輕店員查了查平板。「特價才是對的，貼紙是舊的。不好意思。」

That settled it. Jess also picked out a brass {{lamp|lamp}} and a small blue {{vase|vase}} to go with it. But when they reached the {{checkout|checkout}}, the line wound halfway back to the dining tables, and Tom looked at his watch.
這下他們決定買了。潔絲又挑了一盞黃銅檯燈和一個藍色小花瓶來搭配。可是走到結帳處時，隊伍已經排到餐桌區一半，湯姆看了看手錶。

Nina saw the problem and opened a second register herself. "We're a local {{retailer|retailer}}," she told the people waiting. "We don't want anyone to leave because of a line." Tom and Jess paid in five minutes. Before they left, Omar peeled the old sticker off the arm and handed it over with a grin. It ended up on their fridge.
妮娜看出問題所在，親自開了第二台收銀機。「我們是在地的零售商，」她對排隊的人說，「不想讓任何人因為排隊而離開。」湯姆和潔絲五分鐘就結完帳了。臨走前，歐馬把扶手上那張舊貼紙撕下來，笑著遞給他們。它後來被貼在他們家的冰箱上。
